source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 7 ("Contests in six Belfast wards: fourteen Unionists to be unopposed"); Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 9 ("Belfast City Council: Alderman Midgley, M.P., unopposed in Dock Ward")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed after Robert Semple M'Burnie (Jubilee Protestant Defence Association) withdrew (News-Letter, 7 May 1936)

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934 (no election in January 1935): one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the 1932 cohort) and the eight aldermen elected in 1929 (Clifton, Court, Cromac, Dock, Falls, Shankill, Victoria, Windsor); nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. After the withdrawal in Dock, 17 of the 23 seats were filled unopposed; Clifton, Court (both seats), Duncairn, Falls and Smithfield were contested (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 7 and 16 May 1936). Returned unopposed.
